question:
A 36-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 3-week history of constant low back pain that began
after the birth of her second child. The pain worsens with forward and backward bending. She has no
additional symptoms and reports that her baby is healthy and exclusively breastfed. Physical
examination reveals no tenderness in the thoracic or lumbar regions. Both the standing and seated
flexion tests are equivocal. The sacral bases are symmetrically anterior, and moderate springing of the
sacrum is noted with an anterior force. What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A)
Bilaterally extended sacrum about the inferior transverse axis (B) Unilaterally flexed sacrum about the
middle transverse axis (C) Bilaterally flexed sacrum about the superior transverse axis (D) Bilaterally
extended sacrum about the middle transverse axis (E) Bilaterally extended sacrum about the superior

transverse axis (F) Bilaterally flexed sacrum about the inferior transverse axis (G) Unilaterally flexed
sacrum about the right oblique axis (H) Bilaterally flexed sacrum about the middle transverse axis (I)
Bilaterally rotated sacrum about the vertical axis (J) Unilaterally extended sacrum about the left oblique
axis
 A. Bilaterally flexed sacrum about the superior transverse axis
B. Bilaterally extended sacrum about the inferior transverse axis
C. Bilaterally rotated sacrum about the vertical axis
D. Bilaterally flexed sacrum about the middle transverse axis
E. Unilaterally flexed sacrum about the right oblique axis
F. Bilaterally extended sacrum about the middle transverse axis
G. Bilaterally extended sacrum about the superior transverse axis
H. Unilaterally extended sacrum about the left oblique axis
I. Unilaterally flexed sacrum about the middle transverse axis
J. Bilaterally flexed sacrum about the inferior transverse axis
